title: 登岳阳楼
author: 杜甫
intro: Old, ill and adrift, Du Fu finally sees the great Dongting Lake — a lake so vast it seems to split two ancient kingdoms and float the whole universe. Then he looks north to the war and weeps.
analysis: 岳阳楼在湖南岳阳，下面就是洞庭湖。第一、二句很平淡：从前就听说过洞庭湖，今天终于登上了岳阳楼——多年的心愿实现了。第三、四句写湖的壮阔，是写洞庭湖最有名的句子：吴国和楚国的土地好像被湖水从东南方向分开；天和地、日和月，好像日夜都漂浮在湖面上。“坼”是裂开，“浮”是漂浮，两个字把湖写得无边无际。第五、六句一下子转到自己：亲戚朋友连一封信都没有，年老多病的我只有一条小船。前面的湖有多大，这里的人就有多孤单。最后两句又从个人转到国家：北方关山一带还在打仗，我靠着楼上的栏杆，眼泪鼻涕一起流下来。诗人在自己最困难的时候，心里想的仍然是国家，这正是杜甫被称为“诗圣”的原因之一。
analysisEn: Yueyang Tower stands in Hunan province, looking over Dongting Lake. The opening couplet is deliberately plain: long ago I heard of Dongting's waters; today I climb Yueyang Tower — a lifelong wish fulfilled. The second couplet is perhaps the most famous description of the lake ever written. The ancient lands of Wu and Chu seem to be split apart by it to the east and south; heaven and earth, sun and moon, seem to float on it day and night. Two verbs — 坼, “to crack open”, and 浮, “to float” — make the water seem boundless. Then the poem turns sharply inward. Not a single letter comes from family or friends; old and sick, he has nothing but a lone boat. The vaster the lake, the lonelier the man. The final couplet turns outward again, to the country: war horses still fill the passes to the north, and leaning on the railing, he weeps. Even at his lowest, Du Fu's thoughts go to the nation's suffering — one reason he is remembered as the “Sage of Poetry”.
background: Du Fu (712–770) wrote this in the winter of 768, when he had drifted down the Yangtze to Yueyang with his family, living mostly on a boat. Tibetan forces were then raiding the northwest frontier. He died about two years later.
pronunciation: 坼 chè（裂开）；乾坤 qián kūn（“乾”不读 gān）；涕泗 tì sì；凭轩 píng。
version: 采用通行教材版本，无重要异文。

lines.lit: Long ago I heard of Dongting's waters;
lines.en: For years I had heard of Dongting Lake;
today I climb Yueyang Tower at last.

lines.lit: Wu and Chu, to the east and south, split apart;
lines.en: It splits the old lands of Wu and Chu to the east and south;

lines.lit: heaven and earth, day and night, float.
lines.en: heaven and earth float on it, day and night.

lines.lit: Kin and friends: not one word;
lines.en: From family and friends, not a single word;

lines.lit: old and ill, I have a lone boat.
lines.en: old and sick, I have only a lonely boat.

lines.lit: War horses north of the passes and mountains;
lines.en: War horses still beyond the northern passes —

lines.lit: leaning on the railing, tears and snivel flow.
lines.en: I lean on the railing, and my tears run down.

words.note: 在今湖南岳阳，江南三大名楼之一，今天是著名景点。
现代汉语说“从前”“过去”；“今昔”“往昔”还用。
中国大湖之一，在湖南北部；“湖南”“湖北”的名字就是因这片湖区而来。

words.en: the old states of Wu and Chu
words.note: 春秋战国时的两个国家，吴在东，楚在西，这里泛指洞庭湖东边和南边的大片土地。
生僻字，现代汉语说“裂开”。
现代汉语也说，如“扭转乾坤”。
现代汉语常用，如“漂浮”“浮在水面上”。
代指战争；现代汉语有“戎马一生”。
指边关和山岭，诗词常用。
“凭”是靠着，“轩”这里是窗或栏杆；现代汉语说“靠着栏杆”。
古代“涕”指眼泪，“泗”指鼻涕；现代汉语“涕”多指鼻涕，如“痛哭流涕”。

imagery.name: 楼
imagery.zh: 登上高楼，眼界开阔，也引出诗人对自身和国家的感慨。
imagery.en: Climbing the tower opens up the view — and opens the poet's thoughts to his own fate and his country's.

imagery.name: 水
imagery.zh: 浩大的洞庭湖水，好像能托起整个天地，衬出人的渺小。
imagery.en: Dongting's vast waters seem to hold up the whole universe, making the man look tiny.

imagery.name: 孤舟
imagery.zh: 年老多病，只剩一条小船为家，写出诗人晚年的孤苦漂泊。
imagery.en: Old and sick, with only a boat for a home — the loneliness of his last wandering years.
